## Tips & gotchas

- Use this guide if you need direct ordering from a Dana dealer without explaining part locations. [t130]
- [Partial] Check the trim level and year, as ratios vary significantly between models like the Titan and Pathfinder. [t130]
- The M205 is ideal for those running OR or PRO-4X trims. [t130]
- Note that Titans with the 'big' tow package typically came with 3.36 ratios. [t130]
- [Partial] The M205 appeared in V8s starting around 2006 and continued through at least 2012 on Pathfinders. [t130]
- Armada V8 models also utilized the M205 differential. [t130]
- Look for a transmission temperature gauge and 4WD capability as indicators of the 3.36 setup. [t130]
- The majority of SL models also featured this gear ratio. [t130]
- [Partial] If you have a V8 with an M205, ensure your gear ratio matches the intended use case. [t130]
- [Partial] Stock gearing on Pro-4X is 2.93:1. [t130]
- The 3.36 gears are prevalent in LE and Platinum trims. [t130]
- [Partial] SL models generally follow the majority trend toward 3.36 gearing. [t130]
- The Armada is essentially an SUV version of the Titan featuring an independent rear axle. [t130]
- [Partial] Pathfinder V8s didn't get available until 2008. [t130]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Assuming all V8 Pathfinders have M205s (only 2006+). [t130]
